990101.name: Brackwater Coastal Fishery Landings
990101.description:
Dataset: Brackwater Coastal Fishery Landings.

Landing records of the fictional Brackwater fishing cooperative (2030), joining the vessels' trip logs, the harbour weighbridge, the fuel dock and the first-sale auction, used to set fuel subsidies and quotas. Each row is one fishing trip of one vessel.

Columns:
- distance_offshore_km: distance from the harbour to the fishing ground, in km (typical range 6.79 to 35.4).
- sea_temp_c: sea surface temperature at the fishing ground, in degrees Celsius (typical range 12.9 to 21).
- trip_hours: duration of the trip, in hours (typical range 5.09 to 17.4).
- fuel_liters: fuel used in the trip, in litres (typical range 106 to 423).
- wave_height_m: significant wave height during the trip, in metres (typical range 0.37 to 3.22).
- catch_kg: total catch landed, in kg (typical range 56 to 522).
- ice_kg: ice loaded to preserve the catch, in kg (typical range 33 to 204).
- price_per_kg: average first-sale price at the auction, in currency units per kg (typical range 6.51 to 10.2).

Known relationships: Longer and more distant trips use more fuel and catch a little more; catches are best near 17 degrees and drop in rough seas; more catch needs more ice; prices are higher when catches are small and seas are rough.

990102.name: St. Alder Emergency Department Visits
990102.description:
Dataset: St. Alder Emergency Department Visits.

Visit records of the emergency department of the fictional St. Alder hospital (2031), from the triage system, the bedside monitors and the billing of laboratory tests, used to plan staffing. Each row is one adult visit.

Columns:
- patient_age: age of the patient, in years (typical range 22 to 87).
- heart_rate_bpm: heart rate at triage, in beats per minute (typical range 70 to 114).
- body_temp_c: body temperature at triage, in degrees Celsius (typical range 36.5 to 38.4).
- resp_rate_min: respiratory rate at triage, in breaths per minute (typical range 13 to 24.6).
- oxygen_sat_pct: blood oxygen saturation at triage, in % (typical range 91.3 to 98.4).
- triage_wait_min: time from arrival to the first medical evaluation, in minutes (typical range 6 to 62).
- length_of_stay_h: total time in the department, in hours (typical range 2.3 to 17.3).
- lab_cost: cost of the laboratory tests of the visit, in currency units (typical range 80 to 306).

Known relationships: Sicker patients arrive with higher heart rate, temperature and respiratory rate and lower oxygen saturation; they are seen faster, stay longer and need more laboratory tests; older patients stay a little longer and have slightly lower saturation.

990103.name: Corvo City Bike-Share Stations
990103.description:
Dataset: Corvo City Bike-Share Stations.

Daily station summaries of the fictional Corvo City bike-sharing system (2030), from the docking stations' telemetry and the city weather service, used to rebalance bikes between stations. Each row is one station on one day.

Columns:
- temp_c: average air temperature of the day, in degrees Celsius (typical range 5.79 to 28.5).
- rain_mm: rainfall of the day, in mm (typical range 0 to 8.9).
- wind_kmh: average wind speed, in km/h (typical range 2.5 to 21.1).
- distance_to_metro_m: distance to the nearest metro entrance, in m (typical range 136 to 1.32e+03).
- trips_started: trips started at the station in the day (typical range 24.1 to 144).
- avg_trip_minutes: average duration of those trips, in minutes (typical range 10.8 to 21.6).
- bikes_available_avg: average number of bikes available at the station during the day (typical range 3.5 to 16.8).
- dock_utilization_pct: share of the day the docks were occupied, in % (typical range 50 to 88.1).

Known relationships: Warm, dry and calm days have more and longer trips; stations near the metro are busier; busier stations have fewer bikes left and more occupied docks; stations far from the metro keep more bikes.

990104.name: Pinecrest Water Utility District Meters
990104.description:
Dataset: Pinecrest Water Utility District Meters.

Monthly meter readings of homes served by the fictional Pinecrest water utility (2031), with household data from the customer register and weather from the district station, used to design a drought tariff. Each row is one home in one month.

Columns:
- occupants_avg: average number of people living in the home during the month (typical range 1 to 4.8).
- garden_area_m2: irrigated garden area, in m2 (typical range 8 to 117).
- monthly_rain_mm: rainfall in the month, in mm (typical range 11.8 to 158).
- avg_temp_c: average temperature of the month, in degrees Celsius (typical range 15.3 to 28.7).
- supply_pressure_bar: average water pressure at the meter, in bar (typical range 2.38 to 4.04).
- water_m3: water consumed in the month, in m3 (typical range 7.09 to 23).
- leak_index: leak indicator from night-time flow, higher means more leakage (typical range 0.1 to 2.93).
- water_bill: water bill of the month, in currency units (typical range 26.6 to 70.8).

Known relationships: Consumption grows with the number of occupants and, on warm months, with the garden area; rain lowers garden watering; higher pressure raises consumption and leakage; the bill grows with consumption and leakage.

990105.name: Northgate Telecom Support Center
990105.description:
Dataset: Northgate Telecom Support Center.

Weekly agent records of the fictional Northgate Telecom customer support centre (2030), from the telephony platform, the ticketing system and post-call surveys, used to plan training. Each row is one agent in one week.

Columns:
- experience_months: months since the agent was hired (typical range 3.7 to 46.3).
- calls_per_day: average calls handled per working day (typical range 34.1 to 65).
- avg_handle_min: average handling time of a call, in minutes (typical range 4.53 to 9.16).
- avg_hold_s: average time customers waited on hold, in seconds (typical range 14 to 70).
- first_call_resolution_pct: share of issues solved in the first call, in % (typical range 60.7 to 88).
- overtime_h_week: overtime worked in the week, in hours (typical range 0.395 to 6.3).
- csat_score: average customer satisfaction score from the survey, from 0 to 10 (typical range 6.19 to 8.17).
- absence_h_month: hours of unplanned absence in the month (typical range 0.6 to 5.2).

Known relationships: More experienced agents handle more calls, faster, with shorter holds and more first-call resolutions; satisfaction rises with first-call resolution and falls with long holds and with agent overtime; overtime comes with more absence.

990106.name: Valdeluz Vineyard Harvest Lots
990106.description:
Dataset: Valdeluz Vineyard Harvest Lots.

Harvest lots of the fictional Valdeluz wine estate (2029-2031), with weather from the estate station, vineyard records and the cellar laboratory analysis of the must, used to decide picking dates. Each row is one harvested lot.

Columns:
- sun_hours: sunshine hours in the growing season (typical range 1.2e+03 to 1.71e+03).
- season_rain_mm: rainfall in the season, in mm (typical range 252 to 591).
- vine_age_years: age of the vines, in years (typical range 7.3 to 57.3).
- yield_kg_vine: grapes harvested per vine, in kg (typical range 2.83 to 5.73).
- sugar_brix: sugar content of the must, in degrees Brix (typical range 16.2 to 20.7).
- acidity_g_l: total acidity of the must, in g/L (typical range 6.6 to 8.56).
- must_ph: pH of the must (typical range 3.04 to 3.38).
- alcohol_pct: potential alcohol of the wine, in % by volume (typical range 9.5 to 12.3).

Known relationships: Sunnier and drier seasons give sweeter grapes; heavier crops are less sweet; older vines yield less but sweeter fruit; sweeter musts are less acidic, with higher pH, and give wines with more alcohol.

990107.name: Oriel Running Club Training Log
990107.description:
Dataset: Oriel Running Club Training Log.

Training log of members of the fictional Oriel running club (2031), from GPS watches, a yearly fitness test and a wellbeing questionnaire, used by the coaches to prevent injuries. Each row is one runner in one week.

Columns:
- age_years: age of the runner, in years (typical range 22 to 63).
- body_mass_kg: body mass, in kg (typical range 54.1 to 86.3).
- weekly_km: distance run in the week, in km (typical range 10.7 to 71.9).
- vo2max: maximal oxygen uptake from the fitness test, in mL/kg/min (typical range 40.8 to 59.7).
- resting_hr: resting heart rate, in beats per minute (typical range 52 to 70).
- sleep_hours: average sleep per night, in hours (typical range 5.9 to 8.5).
- avg_pace_min_km: average running pace, in minutes per km (typical range 4.53 to 6.35).
- injury_risk_score: coach's injury-risk score, from 0 to 100 (typical range 16.4 to 43.2).

Known relationships: Fitter runners (higher VO2max) are younger, lighter and run more, have lower resting heart rate and a faster pace (fewer minutes per km); injury risk rises with weekly distance and body mass and falls with sleep.

990108.name: Bramble Mart Store Weekly Panel
990108.description:
Dataset: Bramble Mart Store Weekly Panel.

Weekly panel of the fictional Bramble Mart supermarket chain (2030), from door counters, the point-of-sale system, the marketing budget and stock audits, used to allocate staff and promotions. Each row is one store in one week.

Columns:
- footfall_week: visitors counted at the doors in the week (typical range 2.01e+03 to 8.18e+03).
- competitor_distance_km: distance to the nearest competing supermarket, in km (typical range 1.06 to 7.11).
- promo_spend: promotion spending in the week, in currency units (typical range 135 to 1.95e+03).
- avg_temp_c: average temperature of the week, in degrees Celsius (typical range 6.1 to 29.9).
- staff_hours: staff hours worked in the week (typical range 380 to 719).
- avg_basket: average spend per purchase, in currency units (typical range 27.2 to 45.8).
- weekly_sales_k: sales in the week, in thousand currency units (typical range 37.2 to 173).
- shrinkage_pct: stock lost to damage and theft, in % of sales (typical range 1.06 to 2.71).

Known relationships: Busier stores sell more and get more staff hours; promotions and a distant competitor raise the average basket; sales are footfall times basket times the share of visitors who buy; losses grow with footfall and fall with staff hours.
